mentl/bc8852f:
STAGE 0 of the finish-line plan. The fleet's completeness critic found the
thing that governed everything else: thirty roster items were independently
refuted for having a gate that cannot fail. Thirty authors do not make the same
mistake by coincidence — "a good design has a gate" is a pattern, so thirty
agents emitted gate-shaped text without checking it could go red. Its verdict:
a green board that cannot go red is the most expensive artifact in the repo.

One line caused it. diagnostics_handler saw every diagnostic, printed it, and
resume()d — throwing the severity away. diag_severity has existed all along as a
projection of the DiagKind ADT. The handler knew; the exit code re-derived it as
0. Carried-Truth, at the instrument every other gate reads through.

    check <missing module>   exit 0 -> 1
    check <type error>       exit 0 -> 1
    check <clean>            exit 0     (unchanged — the control)
    compile w/ missing       2432 bytes -> 0 bytes, exit 1
    compile <clean>          2432 bytes (unchanged — the control)

This is NOT a new law. SYNTAX already wrote it, for one class: "a hole is
productive, never executable." That is Hazel's shape, which infer.mn:24 cites by
name — productive at the WALK (a mismatch binds NErrorHole and continues; ten
mismatches yield ten holes, not one-and-halt; unify makes NErrorHole a no-op so
nothing cascades), refusing at the BOUNDARY. The walk's half was built. The
boundary's half was drawn for holes and for decidable-false refinements and
never for the other twelve classes. This reaches them.

Per-class, not all-at-once. The blanket form was designed, dispatched, and
REFUTED on the artifact by three independent verifiers: the wheel reports 2,266
errors about its own source, so refusing on any SError refuses the medium
itself. The target does not lower; the work sequences. diag_refuses names the
ARMED classes — a class arms when the wheel's own census of it is ZERO, so
enforcing it on everyone cannot refuse the medium,

mentl/bcf1fc2:
Parser-conformance cascade #142 — 7 of 14 diagnostics in place:
  E_MissingBracesMultiLine (SYNTAX.md:126-142) — at parse_body's
    non-brace path, check the returned body Node's span; if
    start_line != end_line, emit diagnostic + Quick-Fix.

The check is structurally correct + canonical-clean (T1 single-line +
T2 multi-line-braced don't trigger). BUT empirically doesn't fire on
truly-multi-line bodies (e.g., `fn f() =\n  if x { ... } else { ... }`)
because the body Node's span returned by parse_expr only covers the
first line — substrate gap in span-propagation through compound
expressions (parse_if, parse_match, etc. don't span_join end-line
across nested {...} blocks).

Named follow-up #143 Hβ.parser.span-tracking-multi-line-expr-substrate
captures the span-tracking gap. Once spans propagate correctly, this
diagnostic fires immediately without further parser changes — the
substrate-honest form is in place.

Pattern: lay down the discipline-correct detection; surface the
upstream substrate gap that prevents it from firing. Each closes the
gradient toward end-all-be-all parser conformance.

mentl/bcd2d66:
The IC walkthrough assumed runtime/io.ka had filesystem primitives
— it doesn't. Today's substrate has stdin/stdout/stderr only via
fd_write/fd_read. FS is a small new effect + WASI handler,
mechanically extending the existing io.ka patterns; named here so
the IC commit cluster orders cleanly.

FS is NOT a substrate gap. The γ cascade built the discipline to
add new effects cleanly (H3.1's EffName makes parameterized
effects structural; H1 handles poly dispatch). FS is the first
post-cascade effect landing; it exercises that discipline.

Design captured:
  Four ops: fs_exists / fs_read_file / fs_write_file / fs_mkdir.
    Enough for IC's cache layer. Future additions (list_dir,
    delete, stat) arrive with the surfaces that need them.
  WASI imports: path_open, fd_close, path_create_directory,
    path_filestat_get. fd_read/fd_write already imported, work on
    opened fds.
  Preopen fd 3 as base. Parameterization via `with Filesystem(path)`
    (H3.1) deferred to when audit-driven severance distinguishes
    permissions.
  Bytes as List<Int> in v1. Packed i8 buffer is a follow-up if
    measured to matter.
  wasi_filesystem handler installs in compile's ~> chain between
    wat_stdout and string_table — grants FS to driver without
    leaking it into compiler-internal handlers.

Audit integration: Filesystem becomes a canonical severance
candidate alongside Alloc/IO/Network. `capabilities_for_severance`
gains an entry. A function proven `with !Filesystem` can have its
WASI filesystem imports severed from the output binary — DESIGN.md
10.3's capability severance realized for one of its load-bearing
capabilities.

Scope: ~150 lines, single commit. Lands FIRST in IC cluster.
Order: FS → IC.1 cache.ka → IC.2 driver.ka → IC.3 graph chase
→ IC.4 pipeline/main wiring.

IC walkthrough updated to name FS as a prerequisite, clarifying
that "no new substrate primitive" means FS isn't a substrate gap
(it's an effect extension using established patterns).
mentl/bc6ec96:
Each module owns one thing, exposed through one effect, empowered by
every peer's perfection. No patches — restructure. Every fallback
deleted. Every ~> chain visible on the page.

- types.ka      — vocabulary: every shared ADT + every cross-cutting
                  effect signature. Ownership is Inferred|Own|Ref.
                  show_* chases TVars live via SubstGraphRead.
                  EffRow / NodeKind / GNode / SubstGraph land here so
                  no circular import tangles the foundation.
- graph.ka      — pure machinery: graph_handler with nodes/trail/epoch
                  /next/overlays. O(1) chase amortized. Trail revert
                  powers Mentl's oracle: checkpoint → apply → rollback.
- effects.ka    — Boolean algebra as pure functions. One row_subsumes
                  services every compilation gate. No handlers.
- infer.ka      — InferCtx accumulates fn effect rows in handler state,
                  binds to graph on scope exit (one-write discipline).
                  perform consume at every VarRef. TRefined → verify.
                  All five PipeKind constructors handled.
- lower.ka      — live observer via LookupTy. monomorphic_at is a graph
                  read. Exhaustive match on every LowExpr. New LPerform
                  and LHandle variants for the teaching substrate.
- pipeline.ka   — the spine: compile/check/query/teach/audit each a
                  |> + ~> topology. Owns env_handler, lookup_ty_graph,
                  diagnostics_handler, fresh_for_inference/query.
- emit.ka       — WasmOut effect makes emission a handler you swap.
                  ty_to_wasm through LookupTy. Exhaustive LowIR match.
- own.ka        — affine_ledger with used/used_sites state. ref-escape
                  structural walk. usage classifier for Inferred params.
- verify.ka     — verify_ledger accumulates obligations. Phase 1
                  default; Arc F.1 handler-swaps to verify_smt.
- mentl.ka      — Annotation/Capability/Expl

A Flying fang's first contact with any solid — cover, a walled
boundary, a standing tree, an intact pyre — is now a clean full-energy
ricochet off the surface normal, and the fang stays Flying and lethal,
so banking a throw off a wall into a kill is a real play. Its second
solid contact knocks it Loose. This replaces the old rule where inner
cover dropped the fang on its first touch and only the Pit ring
granted free angles (two of them); one shared wall_bounces budget on
BoomerangMods supersedes the Pit-only boundary_bounces counter.

Bouncy is exempt everywhere: endless ricochet is that pickup's
identity, and it now rides cover as well as the ring. Heavy still
plows through pyres and trees without ricocheting, Multishot
side-fangs still die on their first wall, Phantom still phases, and a
Loose fang still ricochets while it decelerates. Trees still chip on
every contact and fire fangs still ignite them; only the drop timing
moved. Bot threat assessment already keys on the Flying/Returning
states, so a banked fang stays a threat without changes there.
